resources.string: Uno Launcher’s built-in dunes and glass backgrounds, sized for your display.

Allows Uno Launcher’s Home screen gestures to open the system notifications and Quick Settings panels. It also draws the island above other apps so it can be tapped. It does not read screen content or observe activity in other apps.
Changes the image behind Uno Launcher’s Home screens.
Opens Android’s preview to change the phone wallpaper. On its own it does not change Uno’s launcher background.

When on, choosing a background here also sets Android’s home and lock screen wallpaper to the same picture, replacing what is there now (including a live wallpaper). Off by default; nothing leaves the phone.
The glass edge light stays put in the room as you tilt the phone, so the shine moves across the glass. It reads the motion sensor only while Home is on screen. Off by default.
Higher swings the light further for each degree you tilt and makes the rim brighter and thicker.
Takes one color from your wallpaper and uses it to tint the glass, and for sliders, switches and themed icons. It adapts to light and dark, and keeps text readable. Works with liquid glass on or off.
Height widens the glass rim the lens bends; amount sets how far the view behind is displaced; chromatic adds the color fringe at the edges. Turn off liquid glass for a flat look or to save battery.
Swipe sideways anywhere on Home to change pages. Swipe down on the left for notifications, and on the right for the control panel. Swipe up anywhere to open these settings.
All apps always keeps local app search.

Shows the island above other apps with Android\'s \"display over other apps\" permission. The overlay window is exactly the island\'s size, never draws on the lock screen or when the screen is off, and touches outside it pass through.
A liquid capsule at the camera cutout: the time, then a tap expands battery, the top feed headline, and quick actions. It flashes app launches and charging and never overlays other apps.
Save the current Home layout, folders, widgets, layout settings, and your Uno settings.
Restore shows a review before changing Home.
Suggestions use a fixed word list. Nothing you type is learned or stored.
A light tick on touch-down, firmer for the space bar and Return, lighter again for held delete and cursor sliding. It follows Android\'s touch-feedback setting and the Haptics switch below.

A glass-styled keyboard with key previews, accents on long-press, caps lock, a numbers page and a field-aware Return key. It is strictly local: nothing you type is stored, learned, logged or sent, and its code contains no network access (a test enforces that). Suggestions and autocorrect use a word list bundled in the app (English only); they never learn from what you type, never save a word, and switch themselves off in password, email, web address, name and number fields. Backspace right after a correction undoes it, and that word is left alone for the session. There is no swipe typing yet.

Haptics tick on page changes, sliders, the stack rail and the control panel. Sounds are Android\'s own touch sounds: no audio files are bundled, they follow your system Touch sounds setting and volume, and they stay silent in silent mode. Sounds are off by default.
Hides the apps you pick from Home and All apps until Focus is off. Nothing is uninstalled, and your layout is not changed; hidden apps leave an empty spot.
Tinted takes its colour from your wallpaper (change the wallpaper and the icons follow), without recolouring the rest of the launcher.
Themed uses each app\'s own single-colour icon layer where it ships one (Android 13+), in the launcher\'s colours; other apps are washed to match.

When no installed app matches a search, offer to search an app store or the web. Uno only opens the app you choose with your words in it; it never contacts anything itself, and the web search uses that browser\'s own search engine.

The island shows a green camera dot or orange microphone dot beside the pill while any app is using that hardware, like Android\'s own privacy dots, and a red dot while the screen is being recorded (Android 15+, using the normal DETECT_SCREEN_RECORDING permission). It needs no runtime permission: Android tells every app when the camera or microphone becomes busy, without saying which app is using it. Nothing is recorded or stored.
The island flashes when a VPN connects or drops and when a USB data connection starts or ends (plain charging is not announced here). It needs no extra permission and keeps nothing.

The wide pill is for sound that is playing. Paused media stays on the pill for a few seconds, then the pill goes back to its resting size. If it is worth coming back to (it has a title, you are part-way through it and it is longer than 30 seconds), the track stays on the open island for this long. Finished videos and short clips just fade out.

Over other apps the island normally shrinks to a ring round the camera when it has nothing to show, so it does not cover your status bar. With this on it stays as the wide pill, with the battery level on one side. It covers the status bar icons beside the camera.

The open island shows the apps you picked under Control panel & Focus, Shortcuts in the panel (up to five), one tap each, like the app shortcuts in HyperOS\'s island. Long-press the island for tools: timer, stopwatch, flashlight, and Android\'s internet and volume panels. During a call the card has an End button.

The island flashes the name of Bluetooth audio, a headset or headphones when they connect or disconnect. It needs no permission and keeps nothing. Opening the island on a charging phone also shows how long until it is full.

A download, upload or install with a progress bar in its notification shows on the island as a ring round the app\'s icon, with its percentage; open the island for its card. Only the title and the progress are read, never the body text.
While a maps app shows turn-by-turn directions, the island carries the next instruction and the distance or arrival line under it (the navigation notification\'s own title and text). Nothing is kept.

Android 16 apps can post a Live Update for a ride, delivery, timer or navigation. The island shows the app\'s icon and status beside the camera and a card with its progress when open. Only the title, short status, progress and icon are read, never message text; it needs notification access.

While a call is active, the island shows the caller name and elapsed time from the phone app\'s own call notification, and tapping it opens the call screen. The name is read only while the call is running and never stored.
How much a new notification shows when the island drops down for it:
Separate with commas. A match shows only the app\'s name.
Everything stays on this device. Badges count unread notifications per app; the island shows the app\'s name only, never the message.
Shows frame times, jank, the island\'s window sizes and positions, and what hides it. Debug builds only; it never appears in a release.
Asks Android\'s contacts permission. Names are matched on this device and shown below the app results; nothing is stored or sent.

The open island shows this widget under its time and activities, like HyperOS island widgets. It is an ordinary Android widget that you choose and Android asks you to allow; it runs in its own host, separate from Home.
Apps that can use the island

Every app is linked until you switch it off here. A switched-off app\'s Live Updates, progress, navigation and notification cards never reach the island. The time beside an app is how long its notification card stays.
Rearrange Home, add a widget, change the wallpaper, or open settings.
It moves into this widget\'s stack and leaves its spot on Home free.
Dock full • Move an app out first
Move this widget into the six-row grid before resizing.
The system document picker is still open. Return to it to finish, or cancel this operation.
The photo picker was interrupted. Resume choosing a photo, or cancel and keep the current background.
The widget is waiting at its chosen spot. Finish setup to add it, or cancel to remove the placeholder.
Widget settings were interrupted. Resume configuration, or cancel and keep the widget unchanged.
Add a calendar, photos, or another widget.
Sizes that overlap another item are ignored.
That size overlaps another item or extends beyond the page.
This also restores icon layout, labels, search, and status settings.
Widget stacks are not included; their widgets are tied to this phone.
Your selected launcher background photo is not included in layout backups.
Nothing changes until you choose Restore.
A quiet Home screen built for both sides of your foldable.
Checks GitHub every few hours, downloads the new release, and asks Android to install it. Android always asks you to confirm the install.
You can install any version, including older ones. Android may clear saved layout data when an older version can\'t read the newer format.
Tap to place · Hold to drag
Kept only on this device, never sent, until you clear it.
All your feeds are switched off.
Turn one on under Launcher settings > News feed.
Nothing is contacted until you choose a feed, and each choice connects only to the server shown. Nothing is uploaded.
Uno connects directly to the https addresses you add, and only to those servers. Entries are stored on this device. Nothing is uploaded.
Turn on notification access (Launcher settings, Notifications & privacy) to see what is playing.
Turn on "Track title and artwork in media" (Launcher settings, Notifications & privacy).
Play something and it will show here.
Set one in your clock app.
Set a place in Wallpaper & glass, Appearance, to see sunrise and sunset.
The sun does not set today.
The sun does not rise today.
No icon pack is installed. Install one (F-Droid and other stores have many that work with Nova, ADW or Lawnchair) and it will show up here.
A pack replaces the icons it has; apps it does not cover keep their own icon and the style above. Uno reads only the pack\'s list of icons and its pictures, and sends nothing.
Long-press empty space and choose Edit Home: icons wiggle, drag any of them to a free cell, and tap Done.
The pill at the camera shows the time, music, timers and charging. Tap it to open search, the feed and quick controls.
Launcher settings has six wallpapers, glass controls, icon packs, and a style for the island.
A new Molten metal wallpaper: contours of light that bend into one another like glass, in ice blue by day and ember by night.
Island style: pick from eight looks, or import, copy and paste one, under Dynamic island.
Icon packs: choose one under Icons. Menus across the launcher now share one glass style.
New widgets: Media player, Glance, Liquid battery, Photos and World clock.
Theme copied. Paste it into any message; the other person uses Paste a theme.
The clipboard has no text to read.
